intro: When you search for immigration advisors near me, you're likely looking for someone local who can help with a visa, settlement, or a refusal you're facing. Immigration rules are detailed and the evidence requirements are strict, so it's important to find an adviser who is properly regulated for your type of case. We can introduce you to a suitable UK immigration adviser who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for local immigration advice usually need
need_lead: Most people want clear, regulated help with a specific immigration matter, without wasting time on unqualified advice.
needs: You need to apply for a visa, such as a family, work, or student visa, and want to make sure your application meets all the evidence rules.
You are already in the UK and need to extend your stay or switch to a different immigration route.
You want to apply for settlement (indefinite leave to remain) or British citizenship and need help with the requirements.
You have received a refusal and want advice on whether you can challenge it or reapply.
You prefer to deal with an adviser face to face or locally, and want to check they are properly regulated before sharing documents or paying.
context_heading: Check regulation before you share documents or pay
context: In the UK, it is a criminal offence to give immigration advice unless the adviser is qualified and regulated. They must be registered with the Immigration Advice Authority (IAA, formerly the OISC) at the right level for your matter, or be a solicitor, barrister, or chartered legal executive authorised by their own regulator. You can check the IAA's adviser finder or the SRA register before you share any documents or pay any money.

IAA advisers are registered at different levels that limit what they can do, from basic applications to appeals and representation. Ask what level an adviser holds and whether it covers your type of case. Also keep copies of everything you submit, as evidence rules are detailed and you may need to refer back to them.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Tell us the type of immigration matter you need help with, such as a visa application, extension, settlement, citizenship, or a refusal.
Mention your current immigration status and any deadlines you are working towards.
Explain whether you have already submitted an application or received a decision.
Say whether you prefer to see an adviser locally or are happy to work remotely.
Include any particular needs, such as language support or accessibility requirements.
Let us know if you have already checked an adviser's regulation and want us to introduce you to someone at a specific level.
questions: Are you registered with the Immigration Advice Authority, and at what level?
If you are a solicitor or barrister, which regulator authorises you?
Does your registration cover my type of case, such as an appeal or a complex application?
What documents will you need from me, and how will you keep them secure?
How will you keep me updated on the progress of my case?
What are your fees and what do they include?

faqs.q: How do I check if an immigration adviser is properly regulated?
faqs.a: You can check the Immigration Advice Authority's adviser finder for IAA-registered advisers, or the Solicitors Regulation Authority register for solicitors. Always do this before sharing documents or paying any money.

faqs.q: Can iComply give me immigration advice?
faqs.a: No, iComply is not regulated to give immigration advice. We introduce you to a suitable UK immigration adviser who will quote you directly and provide the advice.

faqs.q: What does 'price on application' mean for immigration advice?
faqs.a: It means the adviser will quote you a fee after they understand your case. Fees can vary depending on the complexity of your matter, so ask for a clear breakdown before you instruct anyone.

faqs.q: What should I do if I've already received a refusal?
faqs.a: Keep the refusal letter and any other correspondence, and seek advice promptly as there may be deadlines to challenge the decision. A regulated adviser can explain your options, such as an appeal or a fresh application.

extra_heading: Comparing several local advisers before you choose
extra: Searching for immigration advisors near me, in the plural, suggests you're weighing up more than one option rather than looking for a single name. That's a sensible approach, because fees, waiting times and the level of registration can differ from one practice to another, and a short comparison helps you ask better questions when you make contact.

When you compare, ask each adviser what level they are registered at with the Immigration Advice Authority and whether that level covers your matter, since a basic registration may not extend to appeals or representation. If they are a solicitor, barrister or chartered legal executive, ask which regulator authorises them and check the relevant register yourself. A local adviser who is open about their registration and happy for you to check is easier to deal with than one who is vague.

It also helps to compare how each adviser explains your options and what they would need from you, rather than comparing headline fees alone. Ask for a written breakdown of what is included, whether any Home Office fees are separate, and who will handle your case day to day. Keep copies of everything you send to each adviser, and don't share original documents until you've decided who to instruct.

extra_faqs.q: Is a local immigration adviser always better than one further away?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Being nearby can make face to face appointments easier, especially if you have documents to discuss or need language support. What matters most is that the adviser is regulated for your type of case, so it's fine to consider someone further away if they suit your matter better.

extra_faqs.q: How do I compare fees between several immigration advisers?
extra_faqs.a: Ask each one for a written breakdown of their fees and what those fees cover, and check whether Home Office fees are separate. Because quotes are on application, the figure will depend on your circumstances, so compare what is included rather than the headline amount alone.

extra_faqs.q: Can I speak to more than one adviser before deciding?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, and it can be helpful to do so when you're comparing options. Be clear about what you're asking at each stage, and avoid sharing original documents until you've chosen who to instruct.
